topic: Manager workflow and usability: WCAG 2.2 conformance of the dashboard's interactive and chart elements, alarm-fatigue and ISA-18.2 alarm-state principles applied to the exception report (acknowledge vs clear, shelving), ranch record-keeping and crew-briefing practice, browser-storage limits for acknowledgements and notes, and recommendations for a ~2-minute morning review, a printable crew briefing and acknowledgement semantics.

rules.rule: CURRENT: severity is shown by icon shape plus a text label, never by colour alone (badge() in app.js: octagon=Critical, triangle=Serious, circle=Warning, each followed by the word).
rules.decision_supported: Lets the manager and crew rank exceptions at a glance, including people with colour-vision deficiency and readers of a greyscale printout.
rules.required_inputs: Severity per exception row (computed by findExceptions).
rules.context: Every viewer and every output medium (screen, phone in sunlight, printout).
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: app.js badge() renders ICON[sev] (distinct SVG shapes) followed by the capitalised severity word. My Playwright run read the table cells as text: bySeverity {"Critical":2,"Serious":6,"Warning":2}. On the Chromium print PDF the icons and words survived (page-1 render at 60 dpi shows the icon and 'Critical'/'Serious' words). SOURCE: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 (Level A), quoted by the fetch as 'Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action'. The Understanding page says a specific-colour meaning (e.g. green = valid) needs an additional cue whatever the contrast.
rules.limitations: Charts encode some states mainly by hue. The over-plan grazing segment (--serious) sits next to the current stay (--s1) at 1.25:1 contrast, but it carries a '+3d' text label. Budget bars are red/green but carry +/-% labels and a dollar table, so 1.4.1 is met there through text. In print, the '+3d' label and the gain 'target' labels nearly vanished (see the print rule).
rules.configurable: No. This is an accessibility floor, not a ranch preference.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None. It is a presentation rule.
rules.recommendation: Keep it. Extend the same shape+text treatment to any new state the report gains (Acknowledged, Shelved, Cleared since last review) and to chart annotations, so no state depends on hue.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, W3C Recommendation
sources.supports: Normative text of SC 1.4.1 Use of Color (Level A)

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.1: Use of Color
sources.supports: Colour must be paired with another visual cue. Identifying a specific colour's meaning requires an additional indicator (G14, G111, G205; failure F81).

rules.rule: PROPOSED (current fails): every detail now shown only on pointer hover (tank reading at a time, grazing stay dates and plan, animal tag and ADG, budget dollars) must also be reachable by keyboard and by touch, through focusable marks or an equivalent 'Show data' table.
rules.decision_supported: Lets a manager on a phone in the truck, or a keyboard or screen-reader user, find which animals are slow, when a stay started, or a tank's recent readings without a mouse.
rules.required_inputs: The rows already loaded (water, moves, weights, budget).
rules.context: All users. Especially phones in the field, where hover does not exist.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED (docs/audit/diagnostics/workflow.usability.research.mjs, Chromium via Playwright): "pointerOnly": {"elementsWithPointerListeners": 232, "byTag": {"rect": 37, "circle": 195}, "focusableAmongThem": 0, "keyOrFocusListenersOnElements": 0}. The Tab order reached only the six filter chips (tabStops: All (10), Water (3), Grazing (1), Gain (2), Health (2), Budget (2)). On a phone (390x844, hasTouch), "phoneTapShowsTooltip": false and a gain dot measured {"w": 4.5, "h": 4.5} CSS px. Animal tags of the 6 slow yearlings appear in the exception row text, but the other details are pointer-only. SOURCE: SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A), 'All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface'. Understanding 2.1.1 lists failure F54 (only pointing-device-specific event handlers). Understanding 1.4.13 says content triggered by pointer hover should also be triggered by keyboard focus.
rules.limitations: Understanding 2.1.1 does not say explicitly that hover-only tooltips are 'functionality'. My reading, an inference, is that they risk failing it through F54. Tested in Chromium only, with no screen reader.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None.
rules.recommendation:
Add a
Show data...
under each chart: per tank the last 8 readings, per group the stays, per animal tag/ADG/weight (sortable, slow animals first). This one change also satisfies 1.1.1 and gives the crew briefing its source tables. Optionally make the dots and bars focusable with tabindex=0 and show the same tooltip on focus.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.1.1: Keyboard
sources.supports: All functionality operable via keyboard; failure F54 (pointing-device-specific handlers only)

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.13: Content on Hover or Focus
sources.supports: Content triggered by pointer hover should also be triggered by keyboard focus (cross-reference to 2.1.1)

rules.rule: PROPOSED (current fails): the custom tooltip must be dismissible with Escape without moving the pointer, and hoverable (the pointer can move onto it without it disappearing), or it must be replaced by click-to-pin details.
rules.decision_supported: Lets screen-magnifier and large-cursor users read chart details. Stops the tooltip from covering the data the manager is comparing.
rules.required_inputs: None (UI behaviour).
rules.context: Desktop pointer users; magnification users.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: hovering the first gain dot gave "afterHover": {"shown": true, "text": "H001 (Heifers) | 0.54 lbs/day, Jul 20 to Sep 15 | Now 1169 lbs", "role": "status", "pointerEvents": "none"}, then "shownAfterEscape": true (Escape did not dismiss) and "shownAfterMovingPointerOntoTooltip": false (it vanished when the pointer moved toward it). CSS: .tip { position: fixed; pointer-events: none }. SOURCE: SC 1.4.13 (Level AA) requires 'A mechanism is available to dismiss the additional content without moving pointer hover or keyboard focus', hoverable, and persistent. Understanding 1.4.13 lists F95 (content shown on hover is not hoverable).
rules.limitations: The tooltip follows the pointer, so 'hoverable' may be argued differently. The Escape failure is unambiguous.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None.
rules.recommendation: Add a keydown Escape handler that hides #tip. Either let the tooltip stay while the pointer is over it (pointer-events:auto plus a short hide delay), or switch to click/tap-to-pin details in a fixed panel below each chart, which also fixes phone use.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.supports: Normative SC 1.4.13 text (dismissible, hoverable, persistent)

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.13: Content on Hover or Focus
sources.supports: Intent and failure F95 (not hoverable). Browser title tooltips are excluded, but author tooltips are in scope.

rules.rule: PROPOSED (partly met): each chart needs a short text alternative that states the decision-relevant state, plus a long alternative or data table. Currently the labels name the chart but carry no values.
rules.decision_supported: Lets a screen-reader user, or a printed or text-only briefing, get 'T4 Lone Tree 10%, down 46 points in 24 h' rather than 'Tank T4 level, last 7 days'.
rules.required_inputs: waterStatus, grazingStatus, gainStatus and budgetStatus outputs (already computed).
rules.context: Every chart on the page.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED chartAlts: Water has 8 charts with labels like 'Tank T2 level, last 7 days', withTitleOrDesc 0, withDescribedBy 0, dataTableInSection false. Grazing is 'Grazing rotation by group' with no table. Gain is 'Average daily gain per animal by group' with no table. Budget is 'Percent over or under budget by category' with dataTableInSection true. The water card <h4> does show the current level as text ('T2 Windmill 11.8%'). SOURCE: Understanding 1.1.1 says charts fall under Situation B and need a short alternative plus a long description that 'identifies the type of chart' and summarizes the data, and 'Where possible and practical, the actual data is provided in a table.'
rules.limitations: Labels exist, so this is not a total failure. The gap is the equivalence of purpose.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If a tank has no reading within the sensor-silent window, the text alternative must say 'no reading since <time>' and must not state the stale level as current.
rules.recommendation: Generate aria-label from the same status objects the rules use, e.g. 'Tank T4, Lone Tree: 10% now, dropped 46 points in 24 hours, below the 25% line'. Add the 'Show data' tables from the keyboard rule as the long alternative.

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.1.1: Non-text Content
sources.supports: Charts need a short plus a long text alternative, with the data in a table where practical

rules.rule: PROPOSED (current fails): when a filter chip changes the exception list, announce the result as a status message ('Showing 3 of 10: Water') and keep keyboard focus on the chip. Remove role=status from the hover tooltip.
rules.decision_supported: Lets a screen-reader or keyboard user filter to one area and keep going without losing their place.
rules.required_inputs: Filtered row count; the area name.
rules.context: Exception table filter.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: the only live region is {"id": "tip", "role": "status"} (the hover tooltip). After clicking 'Water' the rows went from 10 to 3, but "liveRegionTextChanged": false, and the live region still held tooltip text. Keyboard: focus was on 'Water (3)', Enter gave "activeElementAfterEnter": "BODY", and the next Tab landed on "BUTTON All (10)" (focus is lost because exceptionsTable() rebuilds the chips with innerHTML). INFERENCE: role=status on a tooltip rewritten on every pointermove will make a screen reader announce hover text repeatedly (not tested with a screen reader). SOURCE: SC 4.1.3 (AA), status messages 'can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus'. Examples include '5 results returned', and technique ARIA22 uses role=status.
rules.limitations: The focus-loss issue maps to focus order and predictability more than to 4.1.3. It is reported here because it breaks the same workflow.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None.
rules.recommendation:
Add

and set its text after filtering. Update aria-pressed on the existing buttons instead of replacing them. Drop role=status from #tip.

sources.title: Understanding SC 4.1.3: Status Messages
sources.supports: SC text, the definition of a status message, the results-count example, ARIA22 role=status, and the failure note on misusing aria-live/alert

rules.rule: CURRENT (passes): pointer targets are at least 24x24 CSS px (2.5.8). Any new acknowledge, note or shelve controls must keep this.
rules.decision_supported: Cuts mis-taps on a phone in a moving vehicle or with gloves.
rules.required_inputs: None.
rules.context: Filter chips today; acknowledgement controls in future.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: desktop chips measured 69.3-92.3 x 30.1 CSS px with 8 px minimum gap, "allAtLeast24": true. Phone (390 px) gave minW 69.3, minH 30.1, minGapPx 8. SOURCE: SC 2.5.8 (AA), 'The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except when...', with the Spacing, Equivalent, Inline, User agent control and Essential exceptions (Understanding page). Chart dots (4.5 px) only trigger hover and do nothing on tap, so they are not activation targets today. If they become tappable, they will fail unless an equivalent control exists (the Equivalent exception would be met by a data table).
rules.limitations: 24 px is the AA minimum. A larger size for gloved or outdoor use is a sensible design choice, but I did not fetch a source for a specific larger figure.
rules.configurable: Larger sizes, yes. The minimum, no.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None.
rules.recommendation: Keep the chips as they are. Build 'Acknowledge', 'Add note' and 'Shelve' as full-width row buttons on phones, at least 24 px tall and comfortably more.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.5.8: Target Size (Minimum)
sources.supports: The 24x24 CSS px rule, the five exceptions verbatim, and the 24 px circle spacing test

rules.rule: CURRENT (passes in Chromium): keyboard focus is visible (2.4.7) and never fully hidden by author content (2.4.11). Pressed or unpressed chip state meets 3:1 (1.4.11).
rules.decision_supported: Lets keyboard users see where they are while triaging.
rules.required_inputs: None.
rules.context: Filter chips; any future sticky header or acknowledgement panel.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: every chip Tab stop gave focusVisible true, outline 'auto 1px rgb(16, 16, 16)'. A 2x screenshot shows a clear white ring around 'Water (3)' (scratch file focus-chip.png). Fixed or sticky elements: ["tip"] only, and the tooltip is non-persistent. Pressed chip fill --s1 vs the card surface is 9.62:1. Unpressed chip border --axis vs fill is 1.61:1, but the chip is identified by its text label, which Understanding 1.4.11 says removes the need for a 3:1 boundary. SOURCE: SC 2.4.7, SC 2.4.11 (a focused component must not be 'entirely hidden due to author-created content'), and Understanding 1.4.11 (state indicators need 3:1; a boundary is needed only if nothing else identifies the control).
rules.limitations: Only the Chromium default focus ring was tested. Firefox and Safari were not tested. Understanding 2.4.7 says defaults must be highly visible and does not guarantee that every browser default passes.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None.
rules.recommendation: Keep. If a sticky 'data as of / counts' bar is added for the morning review, add scroll-padding-top (technique C43) so focused rows are not hidden under it.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.7: Focus Visible
sources.supports: Focus indicator visible in some mode; G165 platform default; F78

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.11: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
sources.supports: Sticky headers are the common failure; C43 scroll-padding; non-persistent tooltips pass

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast
sources.supports: 3:1 for component state indicators; a boundary is not required when text identifies the control

rules.rule: PROPOSED: chart marks a reader needs to make the decision (past grazing stays, the over-plan segment, target lines) should reach 3:1 against adjacent colours, or carry the same information in text.
rules.decision_supported: Seeing at a glance where a group has been, and how far over plan it is, on a dim phone screen or in sunlight.
rules.required_inputs: The CSS colour tokens.
rules.context: Grazing timeline, gain strip and water multiples.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED (WCAG contrast computed from the CSS custom properties): gridlines --grid 1.2:1 against the card surface; zero/axis lines 1.61:1; past grazing stays --bar 1.38:1; over-plan overlay --serious against the current stay --s1 1.25:1; water threshold dashes --muted 5.92:1; gain dots (--s1 at 0.55 opacity) 3.58:1. SOURCE: Understanding 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for graphical objects needed to understand the content, and says this does not apply when labels or values in the chart convey the same information.
rules.limitations: Whether each mark is 'required to understand' is a judgement. Past stays carry pasture-ID text when wide enough, and the over-plan segment carries '+3d'. Gridlines are not needed to read the values.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None.
rules.recommendation: Darken or outline past stays (or add pasture-ID text at every width). Give the over-plan segment a hatch or outline as well as hue. Leave the gridlines faint.

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast
sources.supports: Chart lines, bars and gridlines needed for reading need 3:1, with exceptions when labels convey the information

rules.rule: CURRENT: every exception row carries a defined first response (the 'First step' column), and a condition with no response is not an exception.
rules.decision_supported: Turns each row into something a crew lead can do, and keeps informational status off the attention list.
rules.required_inputs: A response text per rule.
rules.context: Exception report. The principle comes from process-control alarm management and is applied to a daily ranch review by analogy.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: all 10 rows have a non-empty First step, e.g. 'Check for a leak or a stuck float; haul water if it can't be fixed today'. SOURCES: the exida white paper says ISA-18.2 defines an alarm as an indication 'requiring a response', and 'If the operator does not need to respond, there should be no alarm.' HSE CHIS6 says every alarm needs an operator action, alarms without a defined response should be reviewed or removed, and process status indicators should not be configured as alarms.
rules.limitations: The evidence comes from continuous process-control consoles, not once-a-day ranch reviews. It was not validated in ranching.
rules.configurable: The response text is ranch-specific (C). The principle itself is not configurable.
rules.missing_data_blocks: None.
rules.recommendation: Keep. Move pure status (e.g. 'Head on grass 375') out of anything styled as an alert. Document each rule's consequence and the response time it assumes in the rules table.

sources.title: Alarm Management and ISA-18 - A Journey, Not a Destination (white paper)
sources.publisher: exida.com LLC (consultancy). Authors Stauffer, Sands, Dunn.
sources.pub_date: Copyright 2018-2020. The revision history says it was presented in 2010; the document leaves this unresolved.
sources.supports: ISA-18.2 alarm definition 'requiring a response'; the 10-stage lifecycle; rationalization

sources.title: Better alarm handling (Chemicals Sheet No 6, CHIS6)
sources.supports: Every alarm needs a defined operator action; status indicators should not be alarms

rules.rule: PROPOSED: assign severity by consequence of no response and the time available to respond, with about 3 documented levels (e.g. Critical = act today, animals or water at risk; Serious = act this week; Warning = plan at the next gather or month).
rules.decision_supported: Decides what the crew does first this morning and what waits.
rules.required_inputs: Per rule: consequence class and response window. Ranch staffing.
rules.context: All areas. The current mapping puts budget overruns at the same 'Serious' level as a silent water sensor and an overdue vaccination task.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: the current 10 rows are Critical 2, Serious 6, Warning 2. 'Fuel 21% over season to date' is Serious, the same level as 'Tank T6 ... No reading for 42 hours'. SOURCES: exida says ISA-18.2 sets priority by consequence severity and time to respond, recommends no more than 3-4 priorities, and gives roughly 80% Low / 15% Medium / 5% High as a long-run distribution. HSE CHIS6 recommends about 3 levels based on the consequences of failing to respond, with a suggested split of about 5/15/80.
rules.limitations: The 80/15/5 split describes long-run alarm counts at a process console. It does not apply to one day's snapshot or to a synthetic data set with planted problems, so the demo's top-heavy distribution is not itself a defect. The level definitions are the ranch's choice.
rules.configurable: Yes, per ranch (C), but the method (consequence x time) should be fixed and written down.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If the response window for a rule is unknown, show it at the lowest level that is still visible, never silently drop it.
rules.recommendation: Add 'Why this level' (consequence and window) to the rules table. Consider showing budget variances as a separate weekly or monthly review list rather than in the daily attention list.

sources.title: Alarm Management and ISA-18 - A Journey, Not a Destination
sources.supports: Priority from consequence and time to respond; 3-4 levels; ~80/15/5 distribution

sources.title: Better alarm handling (CHIS6)
sources.supports: About 3 priority levels based on consequence; suggested 5/15/80 split

rules.rule: PROPOSED: acknowledging an exception never clears it. Acknowledge records who, when, a note and the planned action. The row stays on the list, marked Acknowledged, until the data shows a return to normal. A condition that clears and later recurs is a new event that needs a new acknowledgement.
rules.decision_supported: Stops 'I saw it' being mistaken for 'it is fixed' (e.g. tank T4 acknowledged at 7 am but still leaking at noon). Shows the crew what is already claimed.
rules.required_inputs: A stable exception_id, ack_by, ack_at, ack_note, and the recomputed condition on every data load.
rules.context: All exception rows, and especially Critical water rows.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: the page has no acknowledge, note or owner control, and the table headers are Severity|Area|What|Problem|First step (hasOwnerColumn false, hasStatusOrAckColumn false). SOURCES: the Ignition 8.1 manual (vendor) treats Active/Cleared and Acknowledged/Unacknowledged as separate conditions, giving four states (Active/Unacked, Active/Acked, Cleared/Unacked, Cleared/Acked). Alarm events 'never transition from Cleared to Active'; a new event is created if the criteria are met again. Clearing depends on the source value, not on acknowledgement. This is my reading of the fetched summary; the page does not literally say 'ack does not clear'. HSE CHIS6 names rapid acknowledgement and routine silencing as nuisance-alarm warning signs.
rules.limitations: The ISA-18.2 normative state diagram itself was not fetched (the standard is paywalled and web search was unavailable). The state model is supported by a vendor manual and by the analogy. Re-alarming when severity escalates is my own design inference, not sourced.
rules.configurable: No for the semantics. The ranch may choose who is allowed to acknowledge.
rules.missing_data_blocks: Without a stable exception_id an acknowledgement cannot be matched to the next day's row, so the row must be shown as new and unacknowledged, never hidden.
rules.recommendation: States: New (active, unacked); Acknowledged (active, acked: who/when/note/owner); Resolved since last review (cleared, unacked, listed once in a 'Resolved' strip); Closed (cleared and acked or verified). If severity escalates (Warning to Critical), clear the acknowledgement (inference). Key the id as area + subject id (tank_id/group/task/category) + rule id.

sources.title: Alarming | Ignition User Manual 8.1
sources.supports: Active/Cleared and Acked/Unacked are separate; four combined states; a cleared event never reactivates and recurrence creates a new event

sources.title: Better alarm handling (CHIS6)
sources.data_years: Milford Haven 1994: 275 alarms in the final 11 minutes
sources.supports: Acknowledging is distinct from acting. Alarm floods and routine acknowledgement are warning signs.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: shelving (temporarily hiding a row) must have a reason, a person and an expiry, and the count of shelved rows must stay visible. When it expires the row is re-evaluated. Permanent removal (e.g. a tank taken out of service) is a configuration change with a record, not a UI action.
rules.decision_supported: Lets the manager park a known item (e.g. 'T6 sensor: replacement radio ordered, checking tank by eye daily') without it vanishing from accountability.
rules.required_inputs: shelved_until, shelve_reason, shelved_by; out-of-service flag in pasture or tank config.
rules.context: Repeated known conditions: sensor outages, planned budget overruns, deferred tasks.
rules.evidence: SOURCES: exida says shelving temporarily hides less important alarms and shelved alarms reappear after a preset time; out-of-service is an administrative, permit-based bypass that may need management approval; and the ISA-18.2 metrics include 'zero alarm suppressions or attribute changes outside approved methods or management of change'. The Ignition manual says shelving always has a duration, new events are blocked during it, and when it ends the alarm re-evaluates its source. HSE CHIS6 lists suppressing alarms from out-of-service plant as a legitimate quick fix. OBSERVED: no shelving exists today.
rules.limitations: Process-industry analogy. Shelving durations suited to a ranch are a management choice (C).
rules.configurable: Yes. Maximum shelve duration per severity (e.g. Critical cannot be shelved, Serious at most 7 days) is a ranch choice.
rules.missing_data_blocks: Refuse a shelve with no expiry or no reason.
rules.recommendation: Show 'N shelved' in the header with a link. Don't allow Critical water rows to be shelved. Write every shelve and unshelve to the shared log.

sources.title: Alarm Management and ISA-18 - A Journey, Not a Destination
sources.supports: Shelving is temporary with a preset time; out-of-service is administrative with approval; no suppression outside MOC

sources.title: Alarming | Ignition User Manual 8.1
sources.supports: Shelving always has a duration and is re-evaluated on expiry

sources.title: ISA18 series of standards (product page)
sources.supports: The current edition is ANSI/ISA-18.2-2016. Shelving is covered in ISA-TR18.2.3; monitoring and audit in ISA-TR18.2.5.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: show how long each exception has been open (first seen), and flag rows open longer than N days as 'standing' for the weekly review.
rules.decision_supported: Separates new problems (act today) from chronic ones (fix the cause, or change the plan or threshold).
rules.required_inputs: first_seen_at per exception_id (needs a history of daily runs or the shared log).
rules.context: All areas. Some rows already embed an age in their text ('Overdue by 15 days', 'No reading for 42 hours', 'Day 24 of a 21-day plan').
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: hasAgeOrFirstSeenColumn false. The age appears only inside the Problem text for some rules, and not at all for water-low, gain or budget rows. SOURCES: exida (ISA-18.2 metrics) sets a target of fewer than 5 stale alarms on any day. HSE CHIS6 says to measure the number of standing alarms and reduce it.
rules.limitations: N (days before a row counts as standing) is a ranch choice. The process-industry stale-alarm metric is a different time scale.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If first_seen is unknown (no history), show 'age unknown', not 'new'.
rules.recommendation: Add an 'Open for' column. Add a 'New since your last review' marker, which needs last_review_at per viewer and is fine to keep in localStorage.

sources.title: Alarm Management and ISA-18 - A Journey, Not a Destination
sources.data_years: n/a (benchmarks based on at least 30 days of data)
sources.supports: Stale-alarm and nuisance-alarm metrics

sources.title: Better alarm handling (CHIS6)
sources.supports: Measure and reduce standing alarms

rules.rule: PROPOSED: the page must state when the data is from (with a time zone) and how old it is, and flag stale data before the manager acts on it. The demo should say it is a fixed fictional snapshot.
rules.decision_supported: Whether today's plan can rely on these readings or someone must look first.
rules.required_inputs: as_of with a UTC offset; per-source last-update times (sensors, weigh-ins, budget month).
rules.context: Every load. Critical for water, where a reading hours old can be wrong.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: meta.csv as_of is '2026-09-30T18:00' ("asOfHasTimezone": false). At run time the data was "ageHoursAtRun": 368 hours old (browser time zone UTC). The header said 'Data as of September 30, 2026 at 6:00 PM.' and "pageMentionsStaleOrAge": false. Per-tank silence is handled (the T6 row says 'No reading for 42 hours'), but there is no page-level freshness check. Because new Date() parses the string without an offset as viewer-local time, the same file maps to different absolute instants for viewers in different zones (inference from JS Date semantics; the displayed text stays 6:00 PM).
rules.limitations: The right staleness threshold depends on the source: sensors update every 6 h, weigh-ins every few months, budget monthly. Not sourced; ranch choice.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If as_of is missing or has no zone, show 'data time unknown' and suppress 'today' wording.
rules.recommendation: Header: 'Data as of Sep 30, 6:00 PM <zone> (N h ago)', plus a per-source line: 'Water: 7 of 8 tanks reported in the last 24 h; weigh-in Sep 15; budget through Sep'. For the portfolio demo, show a 'Fictional snapshot, not live' badge instead of a staleness alarm (D).

sources.title: Alarm Management and ISA-18 - A Journey, Not a Destination
sources.supports: Monitoring and assessment stage; operators need trustworthy, current alarm states (general principle; the paper has no ranch-specific staleness figure)

rules.rule: PROPOSED: acknowledgements, notes and owners that the crew must share cannot live only in localStorage. Use localStorage only for per-device conveniences (selected filter, last-review time, unsent note drafts) and label anything stored there 'saved on this device only'.
rules.decision_supported: Makes sure what the manager acknowledged on the office PC is what the foreman sees on his phone, and that it survives a cleared browser.
rules.required_inputs: A shared store for the acknowledgement log.
rules.context: Any acknowledgement or note feature on a static GitHub Pages site.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: the page writes nothing to storage today ("writes": [], "localStorageKeys": []). SOURCES: MDN says localStorage is specific to the document's origin and protocol (http vs https are different stores), persists across sessions, is cleared when the last private tab closes, and can throw SecurityError when storage is blocked. MDN Storage quotas says data is managed per origin, is best-effort by default (evicted LRU under storage pressure unless persisted), Web Storage is limited to 5 MiB local plus 5 MiB session per origin, and Safari deletes script-created data after 7 days of browser use with no interaction when tracking prevention is on. WHATWG says 'Each site has its own separate storage area' and user agents 'may ... automatically delete stored data after a period of time'. None of the sources mentions cross-device sync; that localStorage is tied to one browser profile on one device is my inference from per-origin, per-user-agent storage.
rules.limitations: navigator.storage.persist() reduces eviction but still does not share data.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If storage throws or comes back empty, the page must still render every exception as unacknowledged. It must never hide rows because of missing local state.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: sensor readings supplement, and do not replace, a daily eyes-on check of water tanks. The briefing should list tanks to check by eye, and the record should capture who checked and what they saw.
rules.decision_supported: Which tanks the crew physically visits today, and whether a 'normal' sensor reading has been confirmed.
rules.required_inputs: Tank list, sensor status, visual_check_at/by/result (manual observation).
rules.context: Cow-calf and grazing operations with remote tank sensors. The source is a BQA cow-calf assessment guide, not a Northern Plains study.
rules.evidence: SOURCE: the BQA Cow-Calf Assessment guide says water tanks should be visually inspected daily for function and cleanliness, with problems reported to management. Its sample protocol cleans permanent tanks at least every two weeks and notes 'Water is the most important nutrient for general animal well-being.' OBSERVED: the current T6 first step already says 'Check the tank by eye today, then the sensor battery and signal', but no data field records that an eyes-on check happened.
rules.limitations: The assessment guide is undated (FY26 file). Daily checking may be impractical on large Plains pastures in some seasons, where frequency is a ranch decision informed by weather, stocking and sensor reliability.
rules.configurable: Frequency, yes (C). The principle that a sensor is not a substitute for a visual check, no.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If no visual check is recorded for a tank in the period, the dashboard should not describe the tank as 'OK', only as 'sensor normal'.
rules.recommendation: Rename the tile 'Water tanks OK' to 'Sensors normal'. Add visual-check capture to the printed briefing and the acknowledgement log.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: the acknowledgement and notes log is an operational record. Keep it append-only and exportable, and retain it for at least 2 years (longer where law requires) if it is used as evidence for BQA. Keep treatment details out of this dashboard.
rules.decision_supported: Audit trail: who knew about a problem, when, and what was done. Supports BQA assessments and staff training records.
rules.required_inputs: The shared acknowledgement log; retention setting.
rules.context: US beef operations participating in BQA.
rules.evidence: SOURCES: the BQA Field Guide says 'The BQA program recommends keeping records for a minimum of two years, or longer as required by laws/regulations' (p. 8, as extracted), with pesticide records 3 years and VFD records 2 years, and also says to 'Record training and education activities'. The BQA Cow-Calf Assessment expects written protocols, a documented training plan and records, and treatment records with product, date, animal ID, dose, route, person administering and withdrawal time. That treatment record content belongs in the health record system, not this dashboard. SDSU Extension runs programming on digital record keeping and EID ('simplify livestock records and improve animal-level data collection').
rules.limitations: Page numbers come from the tool's extraction of the 2026 Field Guide PDF. The BQA National Manual 2026 PDF fetch failed. Retention is a BQA recommendation, not a legal rule for every record type.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If ack_by is missing, store the record as 'unattributed' rather than dropping it.
rules.recommendation: Use an append-only CSV with ISO timestamps including offsets, never rewritten. Export as part of the season records. Name the health-task source system, but don't copy treatment details into notes.

rules.rule: PROPOSED (current fails in print): a one-page printable crew briefing in black on white, large text, grouped by place or route, each item with its first step, a check box and space for a written result. Generated by @media print or a separate 'Briefing' view.

rules.required_inputs: The exception list (filtered to today and this week), owner or route, as_of, print time, and the fictional-data label.
rules.context: Crews working in low-connectivity pastures; mixed-language crews.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: "mediaPrintRules": 0, "pageRules": 0, "printColorAdjust": "economy". The Chromium default PDF (backgrounds off) ran to "pdfPages": 4 on Letter. Measured at 300 dpi, the main text colour (--ink: title, tile values, Area, What, Problem, severity words) printed rgb(158,157,154), 2.71:1 on white. First step (--ink-2) printed rgb(112,111,106), 5.03:1. The faint notes and table headers (--muted) printed rgb(59,58,55), 11.37:1. So the print hierarchy is inverted: the most important text is the faintest. At 150 dpi the gain chart's target lines and 'target 1.0/2.0' labels are near-white on white and practically invisible, the budget legend swatches (CSS backgrounds) are gone, and card shadows print as grey bands. SOURCES: MDN Printing (@media print, @page, beforeprint/afterprint). MDN print-color-adjust says that by default (economy) a browser 'might opt to leave out all background images and to adjust text colors'. The Penn State SOP Writing Guide says to post SOPs at the workplace in text large enough to read while working, laminate them, use pictures because they help regardless of literacy or native language, and write short imperative sentences. Cornell (Skellie 2019) says to post frequently used procedures in plain view, keep grouped protocols in a binder, and translate if needed.
rules.limitations: Print output was measured only in headless Chromium's PDF. Firefox and Safari were not tested and may differ. The extension SOP guidance is dairy-oriented (Penn State, Cornell), and I found no Northern Plains ranch-specific crew-briefing source (web search was unavailable).
rules.configurable: Content grouping (by person, route or pasture) and language are ranch choices (C).
rules.missing_data_blocks: If as_of is stale or unknown, print it prominently at the top ('Data from Sep 30 - check before acting').
rules.recommendation: Add @media print { :root { --page:#fff; --ink:#000; --ink-2:#222; --muted:#444; ... } .chips, .tip { display:none } .card { box-shadow:none; background:#fff } } and a 'Print crew briefing' view. One Letter page. Columns: [ ] | Where (pasture/tank) | Problem | First step | Result / reading / initials. Footer: as_of, printed-at, 'Example Ranch - fictional data'. Optional Spanish column or second page.

rules.rule: PROPOSED design target (not validated): a ~2-minute morning review. Freshness line, then counts ('2 today / 6 this week / 2 plan', 'N new since last review, M resolved'), then the exception list with Open-for and Owner, with charts below as drill-down only.
rules.decision_supported: What the manager assigns before the crew leaves.
rules.required_inputs: Exceptions with severity, first_seen, ack and owner; last_review_at per viewer; as_of.
rules.context: A daily review by one manager; 5-20 open rows on a typical day (assumption).
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: today's report has 10 rows and 215 words in the row cells (rowCount 10, wordsInRows 215), plus 5 tiles. The tiles mix status ('Head on grass 375') with exceptions. SOURCES (by analogy only): Drew et al. 2014 (PLOS ONE) observed 2,558,760 alarms over 31 days in 77 ICU beds (187 audible alarms per bed per day), with 88.8% of 12,671 annotated arrhythmia alarms false positives. The authors recommend tailoring alarm settings and making delays configurable. exida/ISA-18.2 benchmarks put about 150 alarms/day per operator as 'very likely acceptable' and 300 as the maximum manageable, for a continuously staffed console. HSE says each alarm needs a defined response.
rules.limitations: No user testing was done. The 2-minute figure is a design target, not evidence. The clinical and process benchmarks are continuous-monitoring settings and do not transfer numerically to a once-a-day review; they support only the principle that every row should be actionable and duplicate or non-actionable rows removed.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If first_seen or ack data is unavailable, still show the list, with the 'new/resolved' counts replaced by 'history unavailable'.
rules.recommendation: Order: (1) freshness and the fictional label; (2) severity counts and new/resolved counts; (3) the list grouped Today / This week / Plan, each row with Open-for, Owner/Ack and First step; (4) 'Print crew briefing'; (5) charts with 'Show data'. Measure it with a stopwatch test on 2-3 managers before claiming '2 minutes'.

rules.rule: CURRENT: duplicate and stale rows are suppressed by design (a silent sensor is not also judged on its stale level; a group-wide gain problem is not repeated per animal).
rules.decision_supported: Keeps the list short and each row distinct.
rules.required_inputs: Rule-ordering logic in findExceptions.
rules.context: Water and Gain areas.
rules.evidence: OBSERVED in exceptions.js: 'continue; // its last level is stale, so don't also judge it' and 'if (slow.length && !groupLow)'. The run produced exactly one T6 row ('No reading for 42 hours; last level 98.5%') and no per-animal heifer row. SOURCES: HSE CHIS6 recommends retuning nuisance alarms and suppressing alarms from out-of-service plant. Drew 2014 attributes alarm fatigue to 'inappropriate user settings, patient conditions, and algorithm deficiencies'. exida lists 'suppression by design' (advanced design using process or equipment state).
rules.limitations: Suppression by design must be documented in the rules table so a reviewer knows the per-animal list is hidden when the group is flagged. The table already says '(skipped when the whole group is already flagged)'.

rules.recommendation: Keep. When the group row is shown, also give its count of individual slow animals (e.g. 'and 9 animals under 0.5') so information is not lost.

feature_notes:
CREW TASKS AND BRIEFING: The BQA Cow-Calf Assessment expects water tanks to be visually inspected daily, with problems reported to management, plus written protocols, a documented training plan and training records (https://www.bqa.org/Media/BQA/Docs/bqa-cow-calf-assessment-cover-fy26.pdf). The Penn State SOP Writing Guide (Stup 2001) and Cornell (Skellie 2019) support posted, large-text, laminated, picture-supported, translated instructions. The printed briefing should follow that pattern: short imperative first steps, check boxes, and space to write readings and initials, which come back as manual observations (visual_check_*, ack_note). OBSERVED, current print (Chromium PDF, no print CSS): 4 pages, with main text at 2.71:1 on white. The faintest text is the most important (title, tile values, What, Problem). Target lines and labels vanish. Budget legend swatches are lost.

WATER: the 'Water tanks OK 5 of 8' tile is derived from sensor rules only. Per BQA, it should read 'sensors normal' until an eyes-on check is recorded. The T6 silent-sensor first step already says 'Check the tank by eye today'.

CALVING, BREEDING, HEALTH: stay on scheduling and records. BQA recommends keeping records at least 2 years (Field Guide p. 8 as extracted). Treatment record fields (product, date, ID, dose, route, person, withdrawal) belong in the health record system. The dashboard should only link or schedule. SDSU Extension runs digital-record and EID programming (Cottonwood Field Station, Philip SD), the only South Dakota-specific workflow source I could reach.

ALARM FATIGUE AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: the process-industry evidence (HSE CHIS6 2000; exida on ISA-18.2) and the clinical evidence (Drew et al. 2014, PLOS ONE: 88.8% of annotated arrhythmia alarms false positives, 187 audible alarms per bed per day, March 2013 data) support: every row actionable; 3 documented priority levels by consequence and time; duplicates suppressed by design; shelving time-limited and visible; acknowledge kept separate from clear; standing items measured.

MORNING REVIEW: today has 10 rows and 215 words, which is plausibly scannable in about 2 minutes, but this was not user-tested. The missing pieces are freshness and age, new and resolved since the last review, owner and acknowledgement state, and a Today / This week / Plan grouping. Budget variance may suit a weekly or monthly list better than the daily one.

WCAG SUMMARY (observed in Chromium): 1.4.1 passes for severity. 2.5.8 passes for chips (30.1 px tall, 8 px gaps). 2.4.7 and 2.4.11 pass. 2.1.1 is at risk (232 pointer-only chart elements, 0 focusable). 1.4.13 fails (Escape does not dismiss; tooltip not hoverable). 1.1.1 is partial (names without values; only budget has a table). 4.1.3 fails (filter result not announced; tooltip misused as role=status), and focus is lost after chip activation. 1.4.11 is borderline for some chart marks (past stays 1.38:1; over-plan vs current stay 1.25:1), mitigated by text labels.

DIAGNOSTIC: /home/claude/ranch-ops-dashboard/docs/audit/diagnostics/workflow.usability.research.mjs (new file). Run it with: python3 -m http.server 8862 --directory /home/claude/ranch-ops-dashboard & node docs/audit/diagnostics/workflow.usability.research.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8862/ <outDir>. Outputs from my run are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude-ranch-ops-dashboard/c61c6ab5-2745-59d3-9dda-44a2053cd423/scratchpad/audit/research-workflow/out/ (workflow-report.json, print-default.pdf, p300-1.png, hi-3-top.png, focus-chip.png, desktop-tooltip-escape.png).
caveats:
1) WEB SEARCH WAS UNAVAILABLE. All 3 WebSearch calls returned 'web search budget is used up' (shared limit), so no source came from a search result. Every cited URL was fetched directly with WebFetch: W3C, MDN, WHATWG, HSE, PLOS, BQA, Cornell, SDSU and OSHA pages, plus links found on fetched pages (BQA PDFs, the Cornell PDFs via a 302 redirect, and the exida PDF, which was linked from the fetched Wikipedia 'Alarm management' page; Wikipedia itself is not cited as evidence).

2) FAILED OR EMPTY FETCHES: AHRQ PSNet alarm-fatigue primer (client error), Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert 50 (client error), PubMed 24153215 (returned no article content), and the BQA National Manual 2026 PDF (client error). The ISA-18.2 standard itself (paywalled) was not read. Its content is cited only through the ISA product page, the exida white paper (a consultancy, classed as vendor) and the Ignition vendor manual. The 'acknowledge does not clear' rule rests on vendor and consultancy documentation plus analogy, not on the normative ISA text.

3) WebFetch answers are summaries produced by a small model. Quoted strings are as the tool returned them and were not checked against the raw pages. The WCAG 2.2 TR fetch was truncated, so the 2.5.8 exceptions and 4.1.3 text come from the Understanding pages. The exida paper's date is inconsistent (copyright 2018-2020; presented 2010). The BQA Field Guide page numbers come from the extracted text. The BQA assessment guide and several pages are undated.

4) BROWSER TESTING: Chromium headless via Playwright only, with no screen reader and no Firefox or Safari. Print results describe Chromium's PDF output with printBackground off (the dialog default); other browsers may recolour differently. Contrast figures are computed from CSS tokens and from rasterised PDF pixels (300 dpi). No user testing was done; the '2-minute review' is a design target.

5) EVIDENCE TRANSFER: the clinical and process-industry alarm evidence transfers to a once-daily ranch exception report by analogy only. Their numeric benchmarks (150-300 alarms/day; 80/15/5 priority split; 88.8% false positives) must not be read as ranch thresholds. Northern Plains-specific sources on crew briefing or work orders were not found (SDSU covers records and EID only). The SOP guidance is dairy-oriented (Penn State and Cornell).

6) REPO STATE: the local branch HEAD is bff0ba9 (two audit commits after cfd77e5), not cfd77e5. `git diff cfd77e5 HEAD` shows no changes to index.html, app.js, exceptions.js, data/, scripts/, tests/, README.md or .github/, so the app under test matches the reviewed commit.
